title: Declare only a JS/TS-family runtime in a test's Runtime header

facts.note: Authoritative scope: every test file the bun suite actually collects. No path glob is used as a gate; collection by the bun suite decides membership.

values: test file whose header declares a `// Runtime:` field
facts.note: Requires parsing the test file header for a `// Runtime:` comment and its value (bun_tester_discipline_detector does this parse). Applies to the current file state, including unchanged existing headers; no edit-history condition.
Detector finding emitted when the declared runtime is outside the JS/TS family.

fires: Any test file collected by the bun suite carries `// Runtime: python`, whether or not that file or header was touched in the current change.
Any collected test declares a `// Runtime:` value outside bun, browser, isomorphic, typescript, ts, node, js, javascript, deno, vite, astro, preact.
The detector reports BUN-ROUTING-RUNTIME-FAMILY-001 on a test file.
doesNotFire: A test file with no `// Runtime:` field at all (the field is optional for tests).
A test declaring `// Runtime: node`, `deno`, `vite`, `astro`, `preact` or any other JS/TS-family value, even though source files are limited to bun|browser|isomorphic.
A non-test source file's `// Runtime:` header (governed by source-side routing rules, not this one).

given: A test file collected and executed by the bun suite
when: its header declares the optional `// Runtime:` field (any existing or new declaration, regardless of what was edited)
then: The declared runtime MUST be in the JS/TS family: bun, browser, isomorphic, typescript, ts, node, js, javascript, deno, vite, astro, or preact.
prefer: Declare the runtime the suite actually executes under, e.g. `// Runtime: bun`.
Or drop the `// Runtime:` field entirely; the suite's runner is already known from the provider.
If the test genuinely belongs to a non-JS runtime, move it to the suite of that runtime instead of relabelling it.
avoid: Declaring a non-JS runtime such as `python` on a test that `bun test` collects — it is mislabelled or filed in the wrong suite.
Restricting test headers to the source-side `bun|browser|isomorphic` vocabulary; the test vocabulary is deliberately the wider JS/TS family.
unless: The test has no `Runtime:` field — the field is optional for tests and absence is not flagged.
why: Every test file in this stack is collected and executed by `bun test`, a JS/TS runtime, whatever its header claims; a non-JS declaration makes the gate attribute the test to a runner that never executed it.
evidence: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no BUN-ROUTING-RUNTIME-FAMILY-001 finding for any test file collected by the bun suite.
Every collected test file either lacks a `// Runtime:` header or its value is in the JS/TS family list.
verifier_detail: Parse the test file header for `// Runtime: <value>`; judge only files that DECLARE a runtime — files without the field are skipped (the runner is known from the provider).
Allowed vocabulary (js_family): bun, browser, isomorphic, typescript, ts, node, js, javascript, deno, vite, astro, preact — the runtimes `bun test` actually executes under.
Test-side vocabulary is deliberately wider than the source-side `bun|browser|isomorphic`; do not apply the source-side list here.
Term declared_runtime: the optional `// Runtime:` field on a test.
Severity 2; disposition strict (see shared:policy.strict-disposition). Finding id BUN-ROUTING-RUNTIME-FAMILY-001.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun realization mirroring `tester.convex.routing-path`, which makes the same argument for Vitest.

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: If the test genuinely belongs to a non-JS runtime, move it to the suite of that runtime instead of relabelling it.
additions.justification: Makes actionable the source's statement that a `python`-declared test may be 'filed in the wrong suite'; no new obligation.

additions.text: doesNotFire entry for non-test source files' `// Runtime:` headers.
additions.justification: The source scopes the rule to test files and contrasts it with the source-side vocabulary; stating the boundary explicitly avoids misfiring on source files.
